title: A New Generation of Smoke, Combo, and CO Alarms for Today’s Home Projects
summary: Resideo’s Scott Harkins joins the Appetite for Construction podcast to explore how AI-powered HVAC insights help contractors tackle labor, leads, and loyalty.
body_markdown:
**Summary**


How are new smoke and carbon monoxide (CO) alarms improving home safety and simplifying installation?


This article explores how BRK's redesigned Smoke, Combo, and CO Alarms help contractors, electricians, and property managers streamline installation, simplify retrofit projects, and support code compliance. It also highlights homeowner-focused improvements, including clearer LED status indicators, SoftCue™ low-battery notifications, and updated designs that make alarms easier to maintain.


# A New Generation of Smoke, Combo, and CO Alarms for Today’s Home Projects


## Advances in installation design, retrofit compatibility, and homeowner interaction are shaping how life-safety systems are used across residential construction


[Fire and CO safety](https://www.resideo.com/us/en/corporate/newsroom/featured-articles/#f:tags=[Fire%20and%20CO%20safety])


11/19/26


A new generation of residential smoke, combo, and carbon monoxide (CO) alarms are entering the market – developed for today’s residential construction, retrofit, and property management needs. The BRK® family of next generation Smoke, Combo, and CO Alarms represent a comprehensive, ground-up redesign, delivering innovation that better aligns life safety devices with the realities of modern residential construction.


For contractors and installers, meeting code requirements consistently and at scale while maintaining installation efficiency is a constant priority. Inspections, turnover timelines, and ongoing maintenance cycles all depend on having alarm systems that can be installed correctly, replaced quickly, and kept compliant across different residential environments.


The new alarms represent a streamlined product family built to support a wide range of installation environments from single-family homes to large multifamily properties. They also help simplify installation, replacement, and long-term maintenance across projects.


## Built for code-driven coverage


A core challenge for residential construction professionals is specifying the right number and type of alarms to meet code requirements across varied layouts and property types. A simplified lineup enables faster, more confident specification by making it easier to select the right devices, standardize installs, and keep projects compliant. To support that level of consistency in the field, the next generation Smoke, Combo, and CO Alarms were designed to support multiple installation scenarios. The lineup includes wired, battery-powered, and combination units, enabling professionals to match the appropriate configuration to each application and help speed up quoting and installation while on the job.


This becomes even more important as residential construction continues to evolve. Larger homes, open floor plans, and increasingly complex mechanical systems require more thoughtful placement of life safety devices so they can perform reliably across a wide range of building types.


## Faster, simpler installation


With installation speed top of mind, small design improvements can make a meaningful difference across large residential projects.


The next generation platform introduces mounting bases designed to support both wired and battery-only models. By standardizing these components, installers can work efficiently across projects and avoid complications that occur when different alarm types require different bases.


Wiring connectors and mounting systems also help ensure secure installation while maintaining familiar practices electricians already rely on. These workflow improvements may seem incremental, but across large housing developments or multifamily projects, they can significantly reduce installation time and unnecessary callbacks.


## Streamlining retrofit projects


While new construction drives innovation, many installations still occur during replacement cycles in existing homes.


The new BRK alarms ae designed to replace select older BRK and First Alert alarm installations without additional adapters or significant rewiring. This backwards compatibility allows contractors and maintenance teams to upgrade existing properties efficiently while minimizing disruption for homeowners and residents.


## Ease of use for homeowners


Beyond installation improvements, modern alarm platforms are also focused on improving how devices communicate with homeowners.


Traditional alarms often rely on chirp patterns or blinking lights that can be difficult for homeowners to interpret, so these new designs address this opportunity through LED indicators that provide clear visual feedback for alarm status, battery levels, and end-of-life notifications.


The alarms also provide SoftCue™ pre-alert notifications that signal a low battery before it becomes critical, helping homeowners address maintenance needs before disruptive late-night alerts occur. This patented feature not only eliminates disruptive middle-of-the-night night chirping but also provides up to a week of advance notice that the alarm requires maintenance. This extended early warning allows users ample time to address the issue proactively, avoiding unexpected noise disturbances while ensuring the alarm remains fully operational and reliable. This clear line of communication can help reduce service calls related to misunderstood alerts while supporting more consistent maintenance practices that help keep properties up to code.


Paired with a consistent design across Resideo’s family of brands – including Honeywell Home smart products – and compatibility with[BRK® SC5 Smart Smoke & CO Alarm systems](https://www.brkelectronics.com/products/sc5-battery-smart-smoke-carbon-monoxide-alarm-1?variant=46647770284209) , the new alarms deliver a cleaner, more unified smart home experience – transforming traditional alarms into a connected safety network. With built-in wireless interconnect, alarms communicate across the home for fast, coordinated alerts and whole-home awareness. Home safety systems are becoming smart, connected, and intuitive, and this platform brings alarm technology up to speed.


## Designed for modern interiors


Function will always be the top priority, but design considerations for smoke alarms are evolving. Today’s alarms are expected to integrate more naturally into residential interiors rather than appearing purely utilitarian.


The new BRK alarm family introduces a simplified design intended to blend naturally into ceilings while maintaining clearly identifiable interaction points for notifications, testing, and silencing. An optional trim ring can also help cover paint marks or surface discoloration left behind when replacing older or larger alarm models, allowing installers to leave a clean finished appearance during retrofit projects.


These next generation alarms also retain features homeowners have consistently valued. A side-access battery drawer, for example, allows AA batteries to be replaced without removing the alarm from the ceiling.


These types of usability improvements ultimately support the same goal professionals are working toward on every project: making sure alarms are installed correctly, maintained consistently, and remain compliant over time.


Putting the need into perspective, data from the National Fire Protection Agency (NFPA) reinforces what’s at stake. U.S. fire departments responded to more than[328,000 residential fires each year](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/research/nfpa-research/fire-statistical-reports/home-structure-fires) from 2019 to 2023, resulting in thousands of injuries and billions of dollars in property damage. Additionally,[three out of five](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/research/nfpa-research/fire-statistical-reports/smoke-alarms-in-us-home-fires) home fire deaths occur in homes with either no smoke alarms or alarms that fail to operate, while the death rate per 1,000 reported homes is cut roughly[in half](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/research/nfpa-research/fire-statistical-reports/smoke-alarms-in-us-home-fires) in homes with working smoke alarms. These statistics not only highlight the importance of rapid detection but also underscore the need for professionals to specify and install systems that can be trusted to perform reliably across residential settings.


## Built for the long-term


BRK Smoke, Combo, and CO alarms are built to deliver reliable protection for up to 10 years, and this platform was engineered with a strong focus on long-term reliability, intuitive usability, and simplified maintenance, delivering dependable performance homeowners can count on year after year. Manufacturing consistency and supply chain reliability also play a critical role in helping contractors plan installations and maintain compliance – factors that have become increasingly important across the industry.


The BRK alarm portfolio reflects this shift, combining updated UL 217 10th edition detection capabilities with improvements that support installation workflows, ongoing maintenance, and consistent code compliance. As residential design and technology continue to evolve, so will expectations for life-safety devices – making thoughtfully designed alarm platforms an increasingly important part of modern home construction.


For more information about the new BRK alarm product line, including smoke, combo and CO alarm models, visit[brkelectronics.com](https://www.brkelectronics.com/) .
